text:
Maya: Quick question — the latest tier spec says 'Priority Lane' add-on is gated to Commit tiers >= 100k tokens/month. Customer RedLeaf just asked for Priority Lane on a 50k commit. Can we clarify eligibility rules?
Noah: Intent was to keep Priority Lane for larger commitments to protect capacity. But we flagged partner exceptions during sales.
Ellie: For clarity, we should codify three paths: 1) default: commit >= 100k; 2) partner carve: negotiated in contract; 3) trial path: timeboxed pilot (30d) for SMBs.
Maya: I like that. Need to capture launch criteria: how many pilot customers, SLA delta, and cost floor.
Noah: Proposed launch criteria: 3 pilot customers on pilot path, measurable latency improvement (p95) <= 100ms, and billing rule in place (one-off pilot fee or trial credits).
Sam: +1. Also need to decide if Priority Lane requires Dedicated capacity on Dedicated/Private customers or is a logical QoS only. That affects pricing.
Ellie: Tech note: for hosted API we can implement soft-priority routing without dedicated GPUs but will need throttles and traffic shaping. Dedicated would be explicit. We should make this explicit in packaging doc.
Maya: Sales asked what exceptions SalesOps can sign vs what needs Legal approval. Sam?
Sam: SalesOps can approve pilot path up to 3 months and up to 50k additional tokens burst. Anything longer or with credits > $20k needs Legal review. I'll add to playbook.
Maya: Great. Also, what about existing customers migrating tiers? If they already have commit we should allow add-on at prorated rate.
Noah: Agreed: prorate by remaining term. Example clause in contract: "Add-ons purchased mid-term are billed pro-rata for the remainder of the commitment period."
Ellie: Small implementation snippet for billing team, e.g.:
```
if (purchase_date < commit_end) {
  prorated_amount = full_addon_price * (commit_end - purchase_date) / commit_length
}
```
Maya: Perfect. Who owns the UI copy for onboarding when add-on is eligible?
Sam: Product marketing + PM should own messaging. I'll take PM side, loop in @pm-marketing.
Noah: One more edge: grandfathering for legacy customers on older SLA tiers — do we keep Priority Lane free or move them to pay?
Ellie: Recommend transitional offer: 12 months of grandfathered access, then onboard to new addon pricing or convert to equivalent included bundle. Document must list grandfathering start/end dates.
Maya: OK action items: 1) Sam to update SalesOps playbook with exception thresholds (due EOD Friday). 2) Noah to draft pricing clause and prorate example (due Tue). 3) Ellie to add implementation notes for routing options and required telemetry (due Wed). 4) Sam to loop Legal if pilot > 3 months or credits > $20k.
Sam: I'll file the SalesOps PR and tag legal.
LegalBot: FYI legal: Exceptions requiring signature: any contract amendment that increases credit exposure > $20k or extends term beyond existing commitment triggers Legal signature (automated rule created).
Maya: Thanks all — will sync with Sales on RedLeaf this afternoon and confirm whether pilot path fits. :thumbsup:
Noah: If RedLeaf pushes back, offer a 30d pilot with monitoring and a short-term price floor.
Ellie: Also add observability requirement: latency dashboards and per-route token billing must be enabled for pilots.
Maya: Noted. Closing this thread once PRs are linked.
Sam: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sales-playbooks/pull/456 (WIP)
Maya: Leaving a note for launch checklist: pilot acceptance criteria, billing rule, UI copy, SalesOps playbook, legal sign-off if needed, telemetry dashboard.
Noah: Tagging @billing-team for awareness.
Maya: End of thread.
